title: Degree bounded by decision-tree depth
statement: Let $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \{0,1\}$ be a Boolean-valued function, and let $D(f)$ denote its decision-tree depth, the least $d$ for which some decision tree of depth at most $d$ computes $f$. Let $g : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$ be its sign encoding, $g(x) = \sigma(f(x))$, where $\sigma$ sends $0$ to $1$ and $1$ to $-1$. Then $g$ has degree at most $D(f)$: every set $S$ with $\hat g(S) \neq 0$ satisfies $\abs{S} \le D(f)$.
hypotheses_covered: f is a Boolean-valued function on the n-cube
g is the sign encoding of f
D(f) is the decision-tree depth of f
conclusion: every nonzero Fourier coefficient of g is supported on a set of size at most D(f)
replaced:
For every Boolean function $f$, the $\pm 1$-encoding
$x \mapsto \mathrm{boolToSign}(f(x))$ has Fourier degree at most $\mathrm{dtDepth}\,f$,
the minimum depth of a decision tree computing $f$. This is the implication
$\mathrm{DT}(f) \le k \Rightarrow \deg(f) \le k$ used as input to O'Donnell's Lemma 4.21.
